baseline.reproduction: Reverse workbook-rows.patch, build @filens/xlsx, copy dist to tmp/continued-review/workbook-rows-baseline/dist. Restore the patch and rebuild. Run node scripts/benchmark-workbook-rows.mjs --iterations 7 --output <directory>, then node scripts/summarize-workbook-rows-benchmark.mjs --input <directory>/results.json. This patch is relative to the already-optimized CSV parser from the previous round, not repository HEAD.

contentReview.reproduction: Run node scripts/review-workbook-rows.mjs with the reconstructed baseline. Requires the existing tmp/performance-other/samples.json corpus, prepared by scripts/prepare-other-format-benchmark.mjs. It compares complete CSV/XLSX models, first 200-row HTML, 64 generated unordered/duplicate/edited tables, and six source representations without timing.

coverage: CSV and XLSX delayed reads after replacement, abort and destruction
superseded source failures do not override new content/errors
already-aborted input does not start a read
sparse/unsorted/duplicate rows and additions between batches
formula values and final rows in two-sheet browser workbook
scroll position resets on sheet change
existing multiline CSV/final empty record browser regression
validation.testRepair: The old large-sheet unit test mocked scrollTop as read-only. It is now writable, matching a real element, so session cleanup can reset scrolling.
validation.vueCommand: ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run from packages/vue, avoiding fixture regeneration

behaviorChanges: Batch row lookup stores only requested rows, preserving last-duplicate-wins behavior, unordered sparse rows and caller edits.
Shared createSheetTable/appendSheetRows helpers benefit XLSX/CSV and Numbers consumers without changing their DOM.
Session generations and internal abort signals discard stale success/failure results, clear old models/DOM and detach listeners on destruction.
CSV/XLSX parsers check cancellation before reads, after asynchronous reads/decompression and before subsequent parsing.
Switching worksheets resets horizontal/vertical scroll offsets.
limitations: Prepared-model DOM construction only: no input loading/parsing, layout, paint or end-to-end first-preview speedup claim.
Generated fixtures contain two columns and 20,000 or 200,000 stored rows. The sparse fixture occupies 600,000 row positions.
Row batches still scan the complete row array; previously rendered rows remain mounted. This is not windowed spreadsheet virtualization.
Append operations and the 20,000-row control are at or below 10 ms and receive no performance claim, even though raw ratios are retained.
Cancellation cannot interrupt an already executing synchronous XML/CSV/ZIP operation; guards stop later work at asynchronous boundaries.
Engineering A/B only, no peer/SOTA ranking or memory claim. External totals remain 2,604 measurements / 1,064 successful filens runs.
conclusion: For the generated 200,000-row model, first-100-row DOM construction falls from 12.0 to 2.0 ms (6.00x), and for the sparse model from 12.3 to 2.1 ms (5.86x). All table signatures match; eight complete file models and 64 additional generated tables also match. No SOTA label.
